name: Ironhand Workshop Anti-Chafe Augmentation Layer
description:
A base layer designed specifically for augmented individuals, with friction-reducing panels at every common augmentation junction point — shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees. The panels use a slick, medical-grade polymer surface that prevents cybernetic components from abrading natural skin during movement.

A quality-of-life garment for anyone with augmentation hardware that interfaces with remaining organic tissue. Without an anti-chafe layer, daily movement can cause irritation, inflammation, and eventually skin breakdown at augmentation boundaries.
functionality: Augmentation junction protection, friction elimination, skin integrity preservation
what_it_says: Your body is part machine and the parts where those two things meet need protection.
story_hooks: An Anti-Chafe Layer is found with wear patterns for augmentations that don't match any commercially available cybernetics — the wearer had custom hardware that isn't in any registry.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting base layer that hugs the torso and limbs like a second skin. Subtly engineered appearance with visible seam placement at biomechanical stress points. Suggests medical precision rather than fashion — utilitarian but refined.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit throughout, with strategically looser panels at augmentation junction zones to allow movement without binding. Tapers at wrists and ankles.
physical_description.primary_material: High-blend synth-wool base with medical-grade polymer overlay panels at friction points
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost frictionless polymer surface on junction panels; slightly textured breathable weave on primary fabric for moisture management
physical_description.color_scheme: Neutral charcoal grey base with pale silver polymer inlays at shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees — the polymer catches light slightly, creating subtle geometric patterns
physical_description.closures: None — pulls on over head and limbs; designed for quick removal if augmentation maintenance is needed
distinctive_features: Precisely placed medical-grade polymer panels matching common augmentation junctions
Minimal Ironhand Workshop logo (embossed, not printed) on left chest
Micro-ventilation zones along ribcage and inner thighs
Flatlock seams to prevent irritation over augmentation hardware
Slightly glossy finish on polymer zones under certain lighting
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional luxury — expensive enough to signal augmentation investment, practical enough for daily wear by mid-tier augmented workers
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by augmented individuals across all sectors — corpo executives, industrial workers, street mercs, medical professionals. Signals someone integrated enough to afford proper augmentation maintenance gear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained, showing subtle wear at high-friction polymer zones after extended use; rarely visibly damaged but may show faint discoloration on polymer inlays from sweat and daily contact
